title: Skills read the process docs by section, not whole
goal: Every skill that reads kb/_self/maintaining.md, content-rules.md, tools.md, git.md or querylog.md names the sections it needs, and a stdlib command prints one section of a kb/_self doc or SKILL.md by heading, so a subagent reads only those sections before acting

gates.question: How do skills get only the part of a process doc they need?
options: section names in each SKILL.md, read with an existing tool (rag.py show PATH:LINE -n N)
a selfdoc.py section DOC HEADING command that prints one section
split the long docs into smaller files
gates.recommendation: a selfdoc.py section DOC HEADING command that prints one section
gates.answer: a selfdoc.py section DOC HEADING command that prints one section

notes: Baseline census: tool results of 314 transcripts of this project (52 sessions, 262 subagent runs), about 4 characters a token; each result is also re-read from cache on every later turn of its session. Whole-file cat/sed of maintaining.md, content-rules.md, tools.md, querylog.md and the older MAINTAINING.md: about 1.5M characters over about 170 calls; kb-add-topic/SKILL.md read as a file about 62 times (440k characters), kb-research/SKILL.md 13 times (200k). Eight skills open with 'read maintaining.md first, then content-rules.md, tools.md and git.md'. selfdoc.py (stale, map, check) and rag.py show do not print a doc section by heading. Kb facts: public/agents/subagents-vs-deterministic-tools.md:122 (progressive disclosure, DOC S1936), public/claude/skills-and-subagents.md:70 (the skills frontmatter preloads whole skills into a subagent, DOC S2157), public/claude/large-codebases.md:33 (DOC S-4jj4dtg4), public/agents/instruction-and-context-limits.md:114 (DOC S1855). Measure: repeat the census on a comparable sample and compare characters read from these paths.
